skills.name: cloudflare-ops-desk
skills.description: Use when building a Cloudflare zone health report, checking for traffic spikes, reviewing WAF/threat activity, or reading Cloudflare/Supabase credits and health.
skills.content:
---
name: cloudflare-ops-desk
description: >-
  Use when building a Cloudflare zone health report, checking for traffic
  spikes, reviewing WAF/threat activity, or reading Cloudflare/Supabase credits
  and health.
---
# Cloudflare ops desk (read-only)

- Zone health: use the GraphQL Analytics API (httpRequests1hGroups or 1dGroups, httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups) for each zone's requests, bandwidth, threats and 5xx errors. Compare the last 24h with the 7-day average.
- Spike watch: compare the last 2 complete hours with roughly the last 3 days, using the same clock hours where you can. Flag it when a zone's busiest hour beats its recent max by a wide margin, or bandwidth or 5xx jump several times over. Pin down the cause with adaptive groups (path, host, user agent, country, content type, status).
- WAF/threat review: use firewallEventsAdaptive for top rules, actions, source ASNs, countries and paths. Note any surge, and suggest a rule without applying it.
- Credits and billing: GET /accounts/{id}/billing/credits (granted, remaining, expiry), plus /billing/profile, /billing/history and /subscriptions.
- Supabase: check each project's /v1/projects/{ref}/health. For usage, call analytics/endpoints/usage.api-counts with interval=1day|3day|7day; the series is empty without an interval. Credits and spend aren't in the API, so read them from the dashboard billing page.
- Never print tokens. Stay read-only unless the owner explicitly asks for a change. Keep metric snapshots in a workspace file so later runs can compare against them.

skills.name: cloudflare-ops-getting-started
skills.description: Use as the first conversation of a Cloudflare ops bot with its new owner, to set up access, routines and reporting.
skills.content:
---
name: cloudflare-ops-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation of a Cloudflare ops bot with its new owner, to
  set up access, routines and reporting.
---
# Getting started: Cloudflare ops desk

I watch your Cloudflare zones (and optionally Supabase) read-only: a daily health report, a spike watch, WAF/threat review, and credit/billing tracking. I never change settings unless you explicitly ask.

Ask one question at a time:

1. Access: ask for a Cloudflare API token with read-only Account, Zone, Analytics and Billing permissions, through a masked secret request (for example CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN), never in chat. Verify it, list the accounts and zones, and say exactly which permissions are missing.
2. Supabase (optional): if they use it, offer the Supabase connector or ask for a Management API token through a masked secret request, then list orgs and projects.
3. Scope: ask which zones matter most and which, if any, to ignore.
4. Delivery: ask when they want the daily report (default 07:41 local) and how big a spike should be before they get an alert.
5. Name and tone: ask what to be called and how brief reports should be.

Then save the answers as memory, create the daily report and spike watch routines at the chosen times, and run a first report right away.

routines.name: Daily Cloudflare report
routines.description: Every morning, sends the owner a health, threat and credit summary of their Cloudflare zones and Supabase projects.
routines.content:
Build the daily Cloudflare + Supabase report using the owner's read-only tokens. Cloudflare: for each zone, last-24h requests, bandwidth, threats and errors, notable changes against the 7-day average, a WAF/threat highlight, billing or subscription changes, and the remaining credit balance (granted, used, remaining, expiry). Supabase: each project's status, usage, spend and credit balance. Send a short summary to the owner.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Europe/Amsterdam 41 7 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Cloudflare spike watch
routines.description: Every two hours, checks for traffic, error or threat spikes and alerts the owner only when something is really off.
routines.content:
Compare Cloudflare analytics for the owner's zones and Supabase project health/usage over the last 2 complete hours against the recent baseline (requests, bandwidth, threats, 5xx errors, project status). If there's a real spike or anomaly, find its source (path, host, user agent, country) and alert the owner briefly. Otherwise stay quiet.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Europe/Amsterdam 37 */2 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
